body:
Hmm. I'm actually having a hard time reproducing this bug on Windows. I'll try sometime later on KDE Plasma Wayland.

Is there any more information you can provide about reproducing it, possibly on other platforms? I'm using the demo project that you linked, with the only modifications being changing tonemap.tscn to be the main scene.

Maybe a new MRP would be helpful with exact steps to reproduce the bug... it would be surprising to me if it's Linux-specific, but I guess that's entirely possible.

If you're not getting it on Windows, then it might just be a Linux-specific issue. I've been using Godot 4.7 dev 5 on Fedora Kinoite 43 (a Fedora Atomic spin). I've mostly used it on KDE Plasma 6, but I also saw the same bug on GNOME 49.

OK, I can confirm this bug on:

Godot v4.7.beta1 - Fedora Linux 43 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Intel(R) HD Graphics 530 (SKL GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 31.19 GiB memory - Dummy (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

Also happens with 4.7 dev 5 as reported. Also happens with master 320e81846979bd716341e0669231954543c4afbd

I've tried two Windows computers and neither reproduces this issue. I've also tried macOS and could not reproduce this issue.

@ArchercatNEO any guesses why this bug would happen (and only happen on Linux?)

After a bit of testing (and trying to get master to build on my end) I have an idea.

We request HDR on the main window before the wayland event that tells us this is supported is sent. Godot correctly decides to not enable HDR because we don't know this is supported yet. Eventually, we receive an event from the compositor which informs us that HDR is actually supported and we request the rendering driver to enable HDR.

At this point, I think the issue is that no rendering driver swapchain resize happens between receiving the wayland event and quering the colorspace of the swapchain so the swapchain is still in sRGB despite HDR being supported. This means that the rendering driver colorspace is sRGB while we expect it to be HDR so we trigger the enabling HDR failed code and revert to SDR.

The reason this doesn't happen when enabling/disabling HDR afterwards is that the swapchain will be resized between requesting HDR and checking if HDR is actually enabled so the fail code doesn't trigger.

I really should have made a smaller PR introducing something like `RenderingContextDriver::window_supports_hdr_output` so we didn't need to do this dance over whether enabling HDR in the rendering driver actually succeeded or not.

I should note this is *technically* a regression introduced by #118076 since I actually encountered this while developing the original PR. Since at that stage I didn't disable HDR in the rendering driver if it failed, the entire sequence of steps I outlined would happen but on the next frame since HDR was still enabled the swapchain would resize into an HDR swapchain, then the additional "dirty_linear" code would detect that the swapchain actually was HDR and enable HDR on everything again but now that we disable HDR in the rendering driver that doesn't happen anymore. I say technically because the old behaviour was extrememly flaky anyway (as shown by this issue)

I have made a commit https://github.com/ArchercatNEO/godot/commit/8dc81b6e64783bcbacdcaaa6685547405dc9cd2b which fixes this issue, as well as handling that llvmpipe doesn't support 16-bit floats so it cannot perform HDR even on wayland better than current master. I haven't made it even a draft PR because we're in feature freeze and I don't know if it could be merged but I though it would be worthwhile to present what I think a non-flaky solution to the problem would look like.

> I haven't made it even a draft PR because we're in feature freeze and I don't know if it could be merged but I though it would be worthwhile to present what I think a non-flaky solution to the problem would look like.

This introduces no new public-facing features and is specifically a bugfix, so it is suitable for merging during the beta phase. This bug is makes authoring HDR content on Wayland very difficult... And I'm not entirely convinced that it's impossible for this sort of thing to happen with a release export...
